plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: it guarantees winning whenever the value exceeds the second-highest bid (positive profit) and avoids overpaying since the price paid is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Given my value of $25, the optimal action is to bid exactly $25, ensuring truthful revelation and maximizing expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit - I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay less than my value when I do win. There's no strategic advantage to bidding above or below my true value of $18.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and independent private values. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of how high you bid (as long as you win), and bidding your true value ensures you win exactly when it's profitable to do so. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I will bid my true value of $31.
